question.prompt:
Let \(S\) be the sum of all positive real numbers \(x\) for which \[x^{2^{\sqrt2}}=\sqrt2^{\,2^x}.\]

Which of the following statements is true?

solutions.title: Bound and count the roots using AM-GM
solutions.explanation:
Taking logarithms exposes the solution \(x=\sqrt2\) and lets us locate another solution. We must also prove that no additional solutions contribute to \(S\).

Taking base-two logarithms of the given equation gives the equivalent equation
\[
2^{\sqrt2}\log_2 x=2^x\log_2\sqrt2=2^{x-1}.
\]
Its right side is positive, so every solution has \(x>1\). Set \(C=2^{\sqrt2}\) and define the continuous function
\[
F(x)=C\log_2 x-2^{x-1},\qquad x>1.
\]
We have
\[
F(\sqrt2)=C\cdot\frac12-2^{\sqrt2-1}=0.
\]
Also, \(1<\sqrt2<2\) implies \(2<C<4\), so
\[
F(2)=C-2>0,\qquad F(4)=2C-8<0.
\]
Continuity therefore guarantees a second root \(t\) with \(2<t<4\).

To prove that these are the only roots, we will show that \(F\) bends strictly above its chords, using only AM-GM. For distinct \(u,v>1\), AM-GM and the increasing logarithm give
\[
\log_2\frac{u+v}{2}
>\log_2\sqrt{uv}
=\frac{\log_2 u+\log_2 v}{2}.
\]
Applying AM-GM to \(2^{u-1}\) and \(2^{v-1}\) also gives
\[
2^{(u+v)/2-1}
=\sqrt{2^{u-1}2^{v-1}}
\le\frac{2^{u-1}+2^{v-1}}2.
\]
Multiplying the first inequality by \(C>0\) and subtracting the second yields
\[
F\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right)>
\frac{F(u)+F(v)}2.
\]
Repeated bisection now shows that \(F\) lies on or above the chord between any two points: first this holds at their midpoint, then at the quarter points, and so on. More precisely,
\[
F((1-s)a+sc)\ge(1-s)F(a)+sF(c)
\]
for \(s=k/2^n\), where \(0\le k\le2^n\). Such fractions approximate every number in \([0,1]\), so continuity extends the inequality to every \(s\) in that interval.

Suppose there were three roots \(a<b<c\). The chord inequality would give \(F(x)\ge0\) throughout \([a,c]\). Choose \(h>0\) small enough that \(b-h\) and \(b+h\) both lie in this interval. The strict midpoint inequality would then give
\[
F(b)>\frac{F(b-h)+F(b+h)}2\ge0,
\]
contradicting \(F(b)=0\). Thus there are at most two roots, and the two already found are all the solutions.

Therefore
\[
2<\sqrt2+2<S=\sqrt2+t<\sqrt2+4<6.
\]
Hence \(\boxed{2\le S<6}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

solutions.title: Use AM-GM midpoint inequalities and continuity to bound the zeros
